issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The memory profile is internally strained: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits awkwardly with very severe PTSD (PCL-5=80) alongside intrusive, disorganised memory items ('memory forces its way in', 'cannot put memories in order'). Those can coexist, but this level of easy verbal access is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile in this severe presentation.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The appraisal pair 'not doing more to stop what happened' and 'I acted in ways that go against who I am' implies both omission-based guilt and action-based moral injury. That can occur, but without any corresponding memory content suggesting the patient took morally troubling actions, the combination is clinically hard to anchor in the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in notable tension with 'the memory forces its way into my mind' and 'I cannot put the memories in the right order' in a very severe PTSD presentation; this is not impossible, but here it weakens coherence because the memory profile otherwise implies poorly elaborated, distressing trauma memory rather than easy verbal narration.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The paired appraisals 'I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened' and 'I acted in ways that go against who I am' together imply a fairly specific perpetration/failed-responsibility moral injury theme. That can occur in terrorism trauma, but with the rest of the profile there is no supporting threat, trigger, or memory content indicating the patient had an agentic role during the event. As selected, these appraisals are insufficiently anchored to the rest of the formulation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Memory is internally inconsistent: saying he can talk about what happened very easily conflicts with also reporting uncontrolled intrusive memories and inability to put the event sequence in order. That combination is possible in milder cases, but with this profile and very high PTSD severity it is clinically hard to reconcile.

Threat is not internally coherent here: 'Having difficulty concentrating' is a nonspecific arousal/cognitive symptom rather than a threat appraisal item, and it does not fit the otherwise clear danger-focused threat pattern represented by false alarms and waking to check safety. Within this node it pulls away from the threat construct rather than reflecting it.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in strong tension with the other two memory items describing intrusive, poorly organised trauma memory ('the memory forces its way into my mind' and 'I cannot put the memories ... in the right order'). Those latter items imply persistent distress and fragmented recall, making very easy verbal access hard to reconcile in the same profile.

'Having difficulty concentrating' is not a threat appraisal item and does not reflect the threat-related content shown by the other threat items ('react as if in danger' and 'wake during the night to check whether I am safe'). It instead indexes a general symptom and weakens coherence of the Threat node with the formulation's Trigger/Threat links.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The Memory node is internally strained: saying he can talk about the trauma very easily sits awkwardly with severe intrusive, disorganised trauma memory content ('memory forces its way in' and 'cannot put memories in order') in a very high-severity terrorism PTSD profile. This is not impossible, but it is the clearest inconsistency within the selected nodes.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The two moral-injury style appraisals imply he believes he had meaningful agency during the terrorist event and failed morally ('not doing more to stop what happened', 'acted in ways that go against who I am'). For a civilian terrorism trauma in this demographic/role, that agency-heavy pattern is hard to reconcile unless additional trauma details are present. It is not supported by the rest of the selected triggers/threat items.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' sits in tension with 'the memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to' and 'I cannot put the memories of the event in the right order.' Intrusive, disorganized trauma memory can coexist with some ability to disclose, but 'very easily' is a comparatively resolved presentation and is hard to reconcile with the other two memory items in a severe PTSD profile.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened
issues.explanation: The pair of appraisals 'I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened' and 'I acted in ways that go against who I am' implies both omission-based guilt and commission-based moral injury. These can co-occur, but together they suggest a more active role in the event than is otherwise reflected anywhere in the profile. With terrorism trauma and the rest of the items emphasizing victim-like reactions rather than perpetration/complicity themes, this combination is clinically hard to integrate.
